title: Compact observability constraints and stakeholder mapping
body:
Context and goal:

This is a compact working note to align observability signal constraints (cost, retention, cardinality) with stakeholder mapping and dashboard orchestration. The focus is pragmatic: how to keep a lightweight set of operator-facing panels that are useful for fast investigations while respecting query budgets and tenant cost allocations.

Why this exists:
- Many dashboards grow organically: high-cardinality widgets get added, query cost balloons, oncall noise increases.
- We need a repeatable decision model to prune, schedule, and delegate panels before they become high-cost debt.

Key constraints (short):
- Query budget per squad: 200k queries/month (pilot number) for non-critical operator dashboards.
- Trace retention tiers: short (14d), medium (90d), long (365d) with progressive sampling and redaction.
- Cardinality cap on panels: avoid >3 dimensions in a single high-frequency widget.
- Cost SLO for dashboards: no single dashboard should account for >8% of total trace/query spend.

Stakeholder mapping (roles + expectations):
- Oncall Operators (ops-eng): require compact incident playbook panels, high signal-to-noise. Low latency queries. Owner: ops-eng.
- Model/Routing Engineers (serving-runtime): need model-level tokenization and latency slices panels; moderate cost tolerance. Co-owner: serving-runtime.
- Product/Feature Leads: need user-facing SLI dashboards (per-tenant UX metrics) with cohorted retention; lower query frequency but longer retention.
- Platform/Infra: needs capacity / utilization dashboards; can accept aggregated rollups (hourly) to save cost.
- Observability Guild: governance, periodic audit, approves panel lifecycle changes.

Panel classification and lifecycle rules:
- Tier A (investigation-critical): 4–6 widgets max, 1min resolution, auto-trace-linking enabled, aggressive sampling exemption (justified via incident templates). Must have explicit owner and runbook.
- Tier B (health / rollout telemetry): 6–10 widgets, 5–15min resolution, trace-links gated by sampling budget. Owner: feature team.
- Tier C (historical / analytics): up to 12 widgets (more tolerated), 1h resolution, sampled traces only on scheduled probe runs. Owner: analytics/product.
- Lifecycle gates: every panel must record "rationale" and a ticket link. Panels not referenced in incidents or runbooks for >180d get flagged for review.

Sampling policy proposal (cost-aware):
- Baseline trace sampling: 1% global for non-critical traffic.
- Tenant-tier override: enterprise tenants (SLA-backed) get 10% sampling for the tenant's traffic; free-tier stays at 0.1% by default.
- On-demand boost: incident hooks allow temporary sampling increase (x10) for a fixed window (max 2 hours) with auto-roll-back. Requires an oncall annotation.
- Trace retention mapping: short-tier traces store full spans; medium-tier store span headers + top-3 annotations; long-tier store only aggregated span summaries and indexes.

Tagging and naming conventions (to reduce cardinality):
- Use coarse-environment tags: env:prod | stage | dev (do not embed region/service in env tag).
- Use normalized model tags: model:llama-2-13b-chat | model:refined-t5-xxl (no hashed parameters in tag names).
- Tenant id: tenant:tenant-hash (stable short id). Avoid mixing tenant+feature tags in high-cardinality widgets.
- Trace anchors: use trace_anchor:request_id (unique id at session-level) only where needed.

Probe scheduling and collision avoidance:
- Probe windows: synthetic probes run every 5m for Tier A models, every 15m for Tier B, hourly for Tier C. Probe schedule must be offset across regions to avoid microbursts.
- Collision rule: if >3 probes target the same model or host within a 30s window, delay lower-priority probes by randomized backoff.

Dashboard orchestration cookbook (practical steps):
1) Inventory: produce a CSV of all dashboards and panels, owners, last-referenced-in-incident date, monthly query cost estimate.
2) Tagging: annotate each panel with tier:A|B|C and with "cost_estimate_category":low|medium|high.
3) Audit run: Observability Guild runs a quarterly audit (first week of quarter) to prune high-cost stale panels or move them to an analytics-only workspace.
4) Cost cap enforcement: dashboards whose monthly cost > cap auto-create a prioritization ticket and (if untriaged after 14d) move to read-only.

Example panel templates (concise):
- Incident starter (Tier A): "token-latency-99p by model" (dims: model, quantized? boolean). Links: trace for top 5 slow requests. Resolution: 1m. Owner: ops-eng.
- Cache warmth (Tier B): "kv-warmth by tenant cohort" (dims: tenant_cohort). Resolution: 5m. Use sampled traces on probe failures.
- Cost heatmap (Tier C): "query-cost-heatmap by dashboard" (dims: dashboard_id). Resolution: 1h. No trace links.

Decision matrix for retention vs value:
- High-value fast investigation traces (post-incident): keep at short-tier (14d) but export compressed summaries to analytics store for 1y.
- Low-value traces: keep sampling low and only store aggregated statistics (percentiles, error-rates) beyond 14d.

Operational runbook snippets (to include in panel docs):
- If panel query latency > 5s: check panel cardinality, reduce dimensions to 1 and re-run. If still high, escalate to infra for query index check.
- If trace-linking produces sensitive data: follow redaction checklist and reclassify trace tier.

Open questions / action items:
- Define exact per-squad query budget (finance + eng sign-off).
- Implement automatic panel cost attribution by dashboard id in telemetry pipeline.
- Build a lightweight "panel audit" UI for owners to accept / archive flagged panels.

Appendix: quick checklist for new panels
- Do we have a named owner? (Y/N)
- Tier assigned (A|B|C): ___
- Max dims in widget: ___ (<=3 recommended)
- Estimated monthly query cost bucket: low | medium | high
- Linked runbook/incident example: URL or ticket
- Retention tier for linked traces: short|medium|long

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally prioritizes governance + lightweight enforcement patterns rather than proposing sweeping technical changes. The goal is to reduce onboarding friction for teams while capping runaway telemetry costs.
- Feedback needed from finance (cost attribution), serving-runtime (sampling hooks), and legal/privacy (retention/redaction tiers).
